prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, showing how exporter selection and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: I have changed my configuration. In round 1 I proposed two parts: Kiyotaki and Moore (B007), and Melitz alone (B026). I now propose a single part, B026, crediting Melitz and Helpman. Two things drove the change. First, the chair's question about whether the one-person B026 part is acceptable made me re-examine it. Under the three-person cap the Melitz-only part is an artifact of the cap and not a judgment about who made the discovery. Helpman's joint work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI is part of the heterogeneous-firm framework itself, and every B026 proposal in the opening named the Melitz-Helpman pair. A two-part prize cannot hold Kiyotaki, Moore, Melitz and Helpman, so I would have to choose between a clean pair in B007 and a clean pair in B026. Second, on the merits I weigh repeated testing against real data most heavily, because my own work tests theory on hand-collected contracts. By that standard B026 is stronger. Selection into exporting and reallocation across firms have been confronted with firm-level customs and production data from many countries for more than twenty years. Several members, including me, concede that identification of the collateral channel in B007 is less clean than the theory. Melitz (2003) is the originating model. The framework moved trade analysis from industries to firms and gave empirical work a shared language. It is also a distinct later advance from the 2008 prize on intra-industry trade and location with representative firms. B007 remains a clean, original mechanism, and I regard the gap as modest. I rank B007 close behind and name it as an alternative. I did not move because of support counts. B026 has the broadest opening support, but I count that as nothing on merit.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is attribution at the edges. Bernard and Jensen on exporter facts, and Eaton and Kortum on quantitative trade, made parallel contributions that this ballot entry does not credit. A Melitz-Helpman prize could be read as under-crediting the empirical and quantitative strands, and the Committee would have to say why Helpman and not a contributor from those lines is the second name. Some welfare magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions such as the productivity distribution. The 2008 overlap question is real. I find the discoveries distinct but cannot settle it from the written record alone. Choosing B026 over B007 also gives up the mechanism I ranked first at opening. B007 has the sharpest two-author attribution on the shortlist, and this change is a judgment about empirical confirmation, not a claim that B007 is weak. Finally, B012 has the largest policy footprint, and I have not shown that attribution cleanliness should outrank breadth of influence. I use it as a tiebreaker only because B012's credit cannot be cut cleanly to three names.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B026 first with Melitz and Helpman. She treats Redding's quantitative extensions as derivative. She argues that the framework disciplines micro data and has survived replication across countries. She also says she would not call B007 an unreasonable choice.
responses.response: Her argument moves me most. A two-name prize keeps credit on the core discovery, and her point that the claim has held up across countries and datasets is the standard I apply to my own work. I withdraw my Melitz-only version and join the pair. I would add her caution that the citation should honour the theoretical framework of selection and heterogeneity and not claim to cover all firm-level trade research. Leaving out Redding is an attribution judgment, and the Committee should state it openly.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B007 first with Kiyotaki and Moore only. He calls B026 a strong case but says credit is incomplete because Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum are uncredited and Helpman's credit is also spread across the trade-politics entry.
responses.response: I agree that the parallel empirical and quantitative contributors are a real cost, and I weigh it as he does. I do not think Helpman's other agenda weakens his claim here. His credit under B026 rests on the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exporting versus FDI, which belongs to the heterogeneous-firm framework. His other work does not dilute it. I accept that this leaves B007 with the cleaner attribution. I still rank the confirmation record for B026 higher, and I keep B007 as my first alternative. I do not read my move as a verdict against his mechanism.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B007 first. He says the Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism is distinct from the 2022 prize and that B026's second name is uncertain because of the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line. He keeps B026 as an alternative.
responses.response: I accept his argument that Kiyotaki-Moore is a different mechanism from bank runs and deposit insurance. That is why I am not dropping B007 as an alternative. My concern is that the empirical identification of the collateral channel remains weaker than the theory. On the second name for B026, I think Helpman is defensible. The discovery is the theoretical framework of selection, and the cited work with Melitz and Yeaple extends it to the exporting-versus-FDI choice. If the Committee cannot accept Helpman without the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum question being resolved, that is a real argument for Melitz alone. I regard it as a weaker outcome than the pair.

responses.point: Hassler (chair) ranks B012 first with Calvo, Taylor and Woodford. He admits that the strongest alternatives, B007 and B026, have cleaner two-name attribution, and he says in his reply on B026 that its scientific case is stronger than he weighed at opening.
responses.response: I take his point that attribution is the real argument against his own first choice. That is also why I do not treat B012 as preferred. I agree with his separation of Calvo, Taylor and Woodford into distinct elements of the framework. A three-name cut still leaves out the usable policy framework, with Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets on one side and Gertler on the other. I would reconsider if the Committee decided the discovery is the originating nominal-rigidity mechanisms and not the estimated policy framework. His reservation about uncredited trade contributors is fair. I do not think it undermines the pair, because Eaton-Kortum answers a different question from Melitz's selection and reallocation mechanism.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B012 first. In his reply he accepts that the three-person cut is contestable but says the framework's persistence through 2021-23 suggests it was modified more than overturned. He wants the recent-inflation criticism tested directly against evidence.
responses.response: I accept that the 2021-23 episode alone does not overturn the case, and I would not use it as the reason to rank B012 lower. My reasons are attribution and the lack of a clean cut among the credited names. Calvo, Taylor and Woodford are plausible originators, but his own willingness to swap Gali for Taylor shows how loosely the trio is held. Friberg's evidence that micro price data point to state-dependent adjustment, which qualifies Calvo's time-dependent mechanism, also remains untested. A prize needs a result that has been tested against data and held up. B026's central selection and reallocation result meets that standard more directly.

uncertainties: Whether Helpman or a contributor from the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line is the right second name beside Melitz, and whether leaving out the empirical and quantitative strands makes a Melitz-Helpman pair premature.
Whether the selection-and-reallocation advance is distinct enough from the 2008 trade prize. I find it so but cannot settle it from the supplied record.

Whether my move away from B007 reflects a real difference in empirical confirmation or only the gain in attribution from dropping the Melitz-only part. I think it is mostly the former, but the margin is small.
How the Committee should weigh breadth of policy influence (B012) against cleaner attribution and tested evidence (B026, B007), and whether Gali in place of Taylor would change that assessment.

How much of B007's identification weakness is permanent and how much is normal refinement of a three-decade-old literature. I have not verified citations, priority claims or the empirical record beyond the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. None of my listed co-authors (Kaplan, Axelson, Weisbach, Jenkinson, Lerner, Sørensen, Robinson, Martinsson, Thomann, among others) appear among the credited names of B026, B007 or B012, and the profile shows no personal tie to Melitz, Helpman, Kiyotaki, Moore, Calvo, Taylor or Woodford. I disclose that my field of corporate finance is close to B001, which is now only a lower-ranked alternative. I disclose my adjunct position at Chicago Booth, my KVA vice-presidency and my long earlier committee service, including as chair 2016-2018. None of these is a tie to a candidate. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
